entry.title: Sembcorp Industries 1H2026 Result 222222
entry.summary: A resilient first half anchored by growth in renewables and integrated urban solutions, with disciplined capital allocation across the group.
entry.content:
Singapore, 13 August 2026 — The first half of 2026 marked another step in the group's transition from a traditional energy player to a broad-based provider of energy and urban solutions. Performance was anchored by a larger renewables portfolio, a steadier contribution from gas and related services, and disciplined capital allocation.

Highlights of the period

  • Renewable energy capacity continued to grow across wind, solar and energy storage.
  • Integrated urban solutions delivered resilient, recurring income.
  • The group maintained a strong balance sheet to fund future growth.

Our purpose remains unchanged: to do good and play our part in building a sustainable future — while creating lasting value for shareholders and communities.

Growing the transition portfolio

Management reiterated that the energy transition is a multi-decade journey. The group is balancing returns today with investment in the low-carbon infrastructure that will define the next decade: renewable imports, energy storage, and decarbonisation solutions for industry.

Looking ahead

The second half will focus on executing the committed project pipeline, integrating recent acquisitions, and sharpening operational efficiency. The group expects the transition portfolio to contribute a larger share of earnings as new capacity comes online.

entry.title: Sembcorp Receives Conditional Approval for Renewable Power Import Project From Peninsular Malaysia to Singapore
entry.summary: Conditional approval paves the way for cross-border renewable electricity imports, strengthening regional grid resilience and decarbonisation.
entry.content:
Singapore, 7 August 2026 — Conditional approval has been granted for a renewable power import project that would bring clean electricity from Peninsular Malaysia into Singapore, advancing the region's ambition to decarbonise its power mix.

Why cross-border imports matter

Land-constrained cities like Singapore cannot scale renewables alone. Regional interconnection allows clean power generated where land and resources are abundant to flow to where demand is concentrated — a cornerstone of a credible net-zero pathway.

What the project involves

  • Development of renewable generation capacity across the border.
  • Transmission infrastructure to deliver power reliably into Singapore.
  • Progressive commissioning, with capacity ramping up in phases.

The approval is a milestone, not the finish line. Final investment decisions will depend on commercial agreements, grid readiness and regulatory conditions.

entry.title: Sembcorp to Invest in Aster Power, Strengthening Collaboration on Energy Solutions
entry.summary: The investment deepens collaboration on integrated energy solutions and expands the group's footprint in fast-growing markets.
entry.content:
The group has agreed to invest in Aster Power, deepening a collaboration that combines development capability with a strong pipeline of energy projects.

A partnership built on complementarity

Bringing together project development, financing and operations expertise lets both parties move faster on opportunities that neither could capture alone. The investment is structured to align incentives over the long term.

What it signals

  • Continued conviction in integrated energy solutions.
  • A preference for partnerships that de-risk execution.
  • A focus on markets with strong demand and clear policy support.

As the energy transition accelerates, collaboration — not solo execution — is becoming the decisive advantage.

entry.title: The AI Race is Becoming an Energy Race 99
entry.summary: Data centres are reshaping electricity demand. The winners will be those who can deliver clean, reliable power at speed.
entry.content:
Every few decades, a new source of demand reshapes the power system. Electrification transformed factories; air-conditioning transformed cities. Today, artificial intelligence is transforming both — and it is doing so faster than the grid can keep up.

The numbers behind the boom

Training and running large models is power-hungry, and the load is not spread evenly. It concentrates in clusters, arriving in gigawatt-sized steps that utilities plan for over years, not quarters.

Compute is now a power problem. The organisations that solve energy will be the ones that scale AI.

What it means for energy providers

  • Speed matters. Interconnection queues and permitting are the real bottlenecks.
  • Reliability matters. Data centres run 24/7 and cannot tolerate interruption.
  • Cleanliness matters. Corporates increasingly demand low-carbon power.

The opportunity is not just to supply electrons, but to design integrated solutions — renewables, storage, and firm capacity working as one system.

entry.title: Innovative Solutions for Wastewater Treatment
entry.summary: Treating water as a resource rather than a waste stream closes the loop between industry, cities and the environment.
entry.content:
Water is the quiet enabler of urban life. Behind every tap is an energy-intensive, engineering-heavy system that most people never see — and one that is ripe for reinvention.

From disposal to recovery

Modern treatment is less about getting rid of water and more about recovering what is inside it: clean water for reuse, nutrients for agriculture, and biogas for energy.

  • Membrane and biological treatment deliver high-quality recycled water for industry.
  • Energy recovery turns a treatment plant from a consumer into a producer.
  • Digital monitoring catches problems early and cuts chemical and energy use.

Closing the loop

When wastewater becomes a resource, industrial estates and cities can operate with far less freshwater withdrawal — a critical advantage in water-scarce regions.

entry.title: Managing Over 2,000 Solar Sites in Singapore
entry.summary: Scale brings its own challenges. A look at the operations, monitoring and people behind a fleet of thousands of distributed solar installations.
entry.content:
Rooftop solar is easy to imagine and hard to run at scale. Two thousand sites scattered across industrial estates, reservoirs and buildings is not a single power plant — it is a distributed network that has to be monitored, maintained and optimised every single day.

Operations at a distance

When sites are spread across a country, you cannot rely on people driving between them. The answer is data: remote monitoring flags underperformance, and analytics prioritise which site needs attention first.

It is still a people business

  • Technicians who can diagnose and repair across many different setups.
  • Engineers who tune performance and manage grid interactions.
  • Partners who own the roofs and share the benefits.

Technology tells you where to look. People are what fix it.

The bigger picture

Distributed solar turns thousands of buildings into contributors to the grid. Managing that fleet well is what turns an ambitious target into dependable, everyday clean power.
